evidence.note: Built a PyTorch reference implementation (test_ref.py) as the first artifact before any kernel, establishing the oracle milestone with an explicit done-check (it works).

Wrote a correct-but-slow kernel and gated it on the reference via test_compare.py across shapes/masks/cauchy, plus a dedicated N=2048 check — a distinct correctness milestone with a concrete exit test before touching latency.
Only after correctness passed did it launch latency benchmarking against the 10 target shapes, showing clear ordering of the latency stage after the correctness stage.

BF16 optimization attempt was caught failing the 2e-2 tolerance by re-running the correctness check against the reference and was rejected — the exit test localized a fast-but-wrong regression during optimization.

Optimization stage was chaotic: repeated full kernel rewrites cycling through tiled-Triton/bmm/conversion approaches, sometimes benchmarking without re-checking correctness first; not decomposed into per-shape tiling milestones, keeping it below the top anchor.

reasoning: The agent exhibits genuine correctness-first staging: a reference oracle, a correct-but-slow kernel gated against it across the shape/mask/distribution grid, then latency tuning against the 10 timed shapes — with each milestone carrying a concrete exit test that localized regressions (the BF16 accuracy failure was caught and reverted). This meets much of the level-8 description. It falls short of 10 because the optimization phase was opportunistic rather than decomposed into per-shape tiling milestones, risk-sequencing was implicit, and correctness checks were not always re-run before benchmarking, placing the observed behavior at a 7.
